summary: Lo, la, li, le replace a noun that is the direct object, and mi, ti, ci, vi do the same for people in the conversation. The idea that makes it click: take the gender and number from the noun you are replacing, then put the pronoun in front of the conjugated verb, where English puts it after: la conosco, non li vedo, l'ho comprato.

subs.label: gender and number: lo, la, li, le
subs.focus: The pronoun copies the gender and number of the noun it replaces, for things as well as people: il giornale → lo leggo, la pizza → la mangio, i biglietti → li compro, le chiavi → le cerco. A mixed group of people or things is masculine plural: Marco e Anna → li invito. Typical errors of English speakers: one form for every it (la pizza? lo mangio; il libro? la leggo), singular for a plural (i biglietti? lo compro), le for a masculine plural or li for a feminine one. The sentence must name the noun, or show it in a short question before the answer, so that gender and number are certain; choose nouns whose gender is obvious at the level (not problema, mano, foto at level one). Keep the verb in the present or another simple tense here, and before a consonant, so that only the choice of pronoun is decided.

subs.label: l' in the singular only: l'ho visto, li ho visti
subs.focus: Before the forms of avere that begin with a vowel or h (ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno, aveva) lo and la are normally written l': l'ho visto, l'ha comprata, l'abbiamo letto. The plurals li and le are never shortened: li ho visti, le ho comprate. Typical errors: l' for a plural (i ragazzi? l'ho visti; le chiavi? l'ho trovate) and a full plural pronoun where the noun is singular. Use l' as the answer for the singular, but do not offer lo ho or la ho as a wrong option or a wrong judge sentence: they are unusual, not a clear error. Before other verbs that begin with a vowel both forms are in use (lo aspetto and l'aspetto, la ascolto and l'ascolto), so never set one against the other. The past participle after lo, la, li, le always agrees (l'ho vista, li ho visti, le ho viste); write it correctly agreed in every option and every sentence, because its ending is drilled in participle-agreement and must not be the thing decided here. With l' the participle is what shows the gender, so the wrong options should be li or le against l', not lo against la.

subs.label: lo for a whole idea: lo so, non lo capisco
subs.focus: When it or that stands for a fact, a question or a whole sentence and not for a noun, Italian uses lo, whatever nouns are nearby: dov'è la stazione? non lo so; è difficile, lo so; perché è partito? non lo capisco; lo dicono tutti; lo faccio io. Typical errors: la because a feminine noun was just mentioned (dov'è la banca? non la so), a pronoun after the verb or a calque with questo or esso (so esso, non so questo), and li or le. Do not make a sentence wrong for leaving lo out after non: non so is also said. Keep mainly to sapere, dire, capire and fare; with pensare, credere and sperare the answer I think so is penso di sì, so do not build lo items on them. Lo with essere (lo è) is not tested.

subs.label: me, you, us: mi, ti, ci, vi
subs.focus: For me, you (one person, informal), us and you (several people) the object pronouns are mi, ti, ci, vi, placed before the verb: mi senti?, ti chiamo dopo, ci invitano a cena, vi aspetto qui. They are written in full before a vowel as well: mi ascolti?, ti aspetto, ci aiuta, vi invito. Typical errors: the English order (chiamo ti dopo, aspetto vi qui), a subject form as object (Marco chiama io, aspetto tu), ci and vi mixed up, lo or la for the person spoken to. The sentence must make clear who is meant (a name addressed, noi, ragazzi). Te, me, noi, voi after the verb are correct when stressed (chiamo te, non lui), so never offer them as a wrong option. Use simple tenses: in the passato prossimo the participle may agree or not with these four (ci ha visto, ci ha visti), so that ending must never be what an item decides. Formal La is not tested here.

subs.label: position: before the conjugated verb, after non
subs.focus: In a statement or a question the pronoun stands directly before the conjugated verb, and non comes before the pronoun: lo conosco, non lo conosco, Maria non mi saluta mai. In the passato prossimo it stands before avere, never between avere and the participle: l'ho visto, non li ho comprati. Typical errors: the English order (conosco lo, vedo la ogni giorno), the pronoun before non (lo non conosco), the pronoun inside or after the compound tense (ho lo visto, ho visto lo). This sub-point is the home of order items: one pronoun, one conjugated verb, with non or a subject to place as well. Do not use sentences with an infinitive, a modal verb, a gerund or an imperative: there the pronoun can or must go after the verb, and that belongs to pronoun-position.

subs.label: no preposition: lo aspetto, la ascolto, li cerco, lo guardo
subs.focus: Aspettare, ascoltare, cercare and guardare take a direct object in Italian where English says wait for, listen to, look for, look at; pagare also takes what you pay for as a direct object (pago il conto, lo pago io). So the pronoun is lo, la, li, le: aspetto Marco → lo aspetto, ascolto la radio → la ascolto, cerco le chiavi → le cerco, guardo i bambini → li guardo. Typical errors: a calque of the English preposition (aspetto per lui, ascolto a lei, cerco per le chiavi, guardo alla televisione) and an indirect pronoun for a person (gli aspetto, gli ascolto meaning him). Remember that le ascolto is correct when le means them (feminine), so make the antecedent a single man, or plural men, when gli is a wrong option. Do not offer pagare per as a wrong option: pagare per exists in other senses (pago per tutti). Verbs that go the other way (telefonare a, gli telefono) belong to direct-or-indirect.

subs.label: ecco + pronoun in one word: eccolo, eccomi
subs.focus: With ecco the pronoun is attached to the end and written as one word: eccolo, eccola, eccoli, eccole (here it is, here they are), eccomi, eccoci (here I am, here we are). The form still follows the noun: dov'è la borsa? eccola; dove sono i bambini? eccoli. Typical errors: the pronoun in front or written apart (lo ecco, ecco lo), the wrong gender or number (le chiavi? eccolo), and a subject pronoun in a short answer (ecco io for eccomi). Ecco followed by a noun is of course correct (ecco il treno) and can appear as a correct judge sentence. Do not use eccoti and eccovi: there the pronoun usually means to you (eccoti il resto), which is not a direct object.

subs.label: object first, then the pronoun: il pane lo compro io
subs.focus: Italian often starts a sentence with the definite object it is talking about and then repeats it with a pronoun before the verb: il pane lo compro io, la spesa la facciamo domani, i piatti li lava Marco, le chiavi le ho lasciate a casa. English has nothing like it, so learners choose the wrong form (la spesa lo facciamo domani, i piatti lo lava Marco) or put the pronoun after the verb. Test the choice among lo, la, li, le and the word order. Do not present the sentence without the pronoun as wrong in a judge item or as a wrong option: with strong contrast on the object it can be said (il pane compro, non il latte). Use definite nouns only (il, la, questo, a possessive); with quantities and indefinite objects the pronoun is ne, which belongs to ci-and-ne. In the passato prossimo keep the participle correctly agreed.

rules.rule: Choose the pronoun by the noun it replaces: lo for masculine singular, la for feminine singular, li for masculine plural, le for feminine plural. Things have gender too, so it is lo or la, and them is li or le.
rules.pattern: il libro → lo | la pizza → la | i biglietti → li | le chiavi → le

examples.tl: Il giornale? Lo leggo ogni mattina.
examples.en: The newspaper? I read it every morning.

examples.tl: Conosci Maria? Sì, la conosco bene.
examples.en: Do you know Maria? Yes, I know her well.

examples.tl: Compri tu i biglietti? Sì, li compro stasera.
examples.en: Are you buying the tickets? Yes, I am buying them tonight.

examples.tl: Dove sono le mie scarpe? Non le trovo.
examples.en: Where are my shoes? I cannot find them.

rules.note: A group with at least one masculine member is li: Marco e Anna? Li vedo domani.

rules.rule: Before ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno write l' for lo and la. Never shorten li and le.
rules.pattern: lo / la + ho → l'ho | li ho, le ho stay whole

examples.tl: Hai visto Paolo? Sì, l'ho visto ieri.
examples.en: Have you seen Paolo? Yes, I saw him yesterday.

examples.tl: La pizza era buona, l'ho mangiata tutta.
examples.en: The pizza was good, I ate all of it.

examples.tl: I tuoi amici? Li ho incontrati al bar.
examples.en: Your friends? I met them at the café.

examples.tl: Le tue amiche? Le ho invitate alla festa.
examples.en: Your friends? I have invited them to the party.

rules.note: After lo, la, li, le the participle takes the ending of the pronoun: l'ho visto, l'ho vista, li ho visti, le ho viste. Before other verbs that start with a vowel you can write lo aspetto or l'aspetto.

rules.rule: When it or that means a fact or a whole sentence, not a noun, use lo. The nouns nearby do not matter.
rules.pattern: lo so | non lo so | non lo capisco | lo dicono tutti | lo faccio io

examples.tl: Dov'è la stazione? Non lo so.
examples.en: Where is the station? I do not know.

examples.tl: È tardi, lo so, ma devo finire.
examples.en: It is late, I know, but I have to finish.

examples.tl: Perché è andato via? Non lo capisco.
examples.en: Why did he leave? I do not understand it.

examples.tl: Lo dicono tutti: è un bel film.
examples.en: Everybody says so: it is a good film.

rules.note: English often says nothing here (I know); Italian likes lo so. I think so is penso di sì, not a sentence with lo.

rules.rule: Me, you, us, you all as objects are mi, ti, ci, vi, and they go before the verb like lo and la.
rules.pattern: mi vede | ti chiamo | ci invitano | vi aspetto

examples.tl: Mi senti? Qui c'è molto rumore.
examples.en: Can you hear me? It is very noisy here.

examples.tl: Ti chiamo domani mattina.
examples.en: I will call you tomorrow morning.

examples.tl: I nonni ci invitano a pranzo domenica.
examples.en: Our grandparents are inviting us to lunch on Sunday.

examples.tl: Ragazzi, vi aspetto davanti al cinema.
examples.en: Guys, I will wait for you in front of the cinema.

rules.note: The stressed forms me, te, noi, voi follow the verb and are kept for contrast: chiamo te, non lui.

rules.rule: Put the pronoun directly before the conjugated verb. Non goes before the pronoun.
rules.pattern: subject + (non) + pronoun + verb: Maria non lo conosce

examples.tl: Non lo conosco bene.
examples.en: I do not know him well.

examples.tl: Maria non mi saluta mai.
examples.en: Maria never says hello to me.

examples.tl: Questa serie è bellissima, la guardo ogni sera.
examples.en: This series is wonderful, I watch it every evening.

rules.note: With an infinitive, a modal verb or an imperative the pronoun can go after the verb (voglio vederlo, guardalo): see the topic on pronoun position.

rules.rule: In the passato prossimo the pronoun goes before avere, never between avere and the participle.
rules.pattern: (non) + pronoun + avere + participle: non l'ho visto | li abbiamo comprati

examples.tl: Il film? L'abbiamo visto sabato.
examples.en: The film? We saw it on Saturday.

examples.tl: Le chiavi? Non le ho prese.
examples.en: The keys? I did not take them.

examples.tl: Cerco Giulia, ma non l'ho trovata.
examples.en: I am looking for Giulia, but I have not found her.

rules.rule: Aspettare, ascoltare, cercare and guardare take their object with no preposition, so wait for him, listen to it, look for them, look at her use lo, la, li, le. Pagare works the same way for the thing you pay for.
rules.pattern: aspetto Luca → lo aspetto | ascolto la radio → la ascolto | cerco le chiavi → le cerco | pago il conto → lo pago

examples.tl: Dov'è Luca? Lo aspetto da un'ora.
examples.en: Where is Luca? I have been waiting for him for an hour.

examples.tl: Questa canzone è bellissima, la ascolto sempre.
examples.en: This song is beautiful, I listen to it all the time.

examples.tl: Ho perso gli occhiali, li cerco da stamattina.
examples.en: I have lost my glasses, I have been looking for them since this morning.

examples.tl: La partita comincia adesso, la guardiamo insieme?
examples.en: The match is starting now, shall we watch it together?

rules.note: Do not translate for, to, at: no per, no a. Some verbs go the other way, such as telefonare a: see the topic on direct or indirect.

rules.rule: After ecco, attach the pronoun to the end and write one word. The pronoun still follows the gender and number of the noun.
rules.pattern: eccolo | eccola | eccoli | eccole | eccomi | eccoci

examples.tl: Dov'è il mio telefono? Eccolo, è sul divano.
examples.en: Where is my phone? Here it is, it is on the sofa.

examples.tl: Cerchi le chiavi? Eccole qui.
examples.en: Are you looking for the keys? Here they are.

examples.tl: Eccomi, scusate il ritardo!
examples.en: Here I am, sorry I am late!

examples.tl: Eccoci finalmente a casa.
examples.en: Here we are, home at last.

rules.note: With a noun, ecco stands alone: ecco il treno.

rules.rule: When a definite object comes first in the sentence, repeat it with the matching pronoun before the verb.
rules.pattern: il pane lo compro io | la spesa la facciamo domani | i piatti li lava Marco | le chiavi le ho lasciate a casa

examples.tl: Il caffè lo pago io.
examples.en: I am paying for the coffee.

examples.tl: La spesa la facciamo domani.
examples.en: We will do the shopping tomorrow.

examples.tl: I piatti li lava Marco.
examples.en: Marco is washing the dishes.

examples.tl: Le chiavi le ho lasciate a casa.
examples.en: I left the keys at home.

rules.note: English cannot do this; Italian does it all the time to say what the sentence is about. The pronoun has the form of the noun in front.

contrasts.wrong: Conosci Maria? Sì, lo conosco bene.

right.tl: Conosci Maria? Sì, la conosco bene.
right.en: Do you know Maria? Yes, I know her well.

contrasts.why: The pronoun copies the noun it replaces. Maria is feminine singular, so la; lo would be a man or a masculine thing.

contrasts.wrong: Compri tu i biglietti? Sì, lo compro stasera.

right.tl: Compri tu i biglietti? Sì, li compro stasera.
right.en: Are you buying the tickets? Yes, I am buying them tonight.

contrasts.why: I biglietti is masculine plural, so them is li. Lo stands for one masculine noun only.

contrasts.wrong: I tuoi amici? L'ho incontrati al bar.

right.tl: I tuoi amici? Li ho incontrati al bar.
right.en: Your friends? I met them at the café.

contrasts.why: Only the singular lo and la shorten to l' before ho. The plurals li and le are always written whole: li ho incontrati.

contrasts.wrong: Dov'è la stazione? Non la so.

right.tl: Dov'è la stazione? Non lo so.
right.en: Where is the station? I do not know.

contrasts.why: What you do not know is the answer to the question, a whole idea, not the noun stazione. For an idea the pronoun is lo.

right.en: I will call you tomorrow morning.

contrasts.why: Mi, ti, ci, vi cannot follow a conjugated verb as you does in English. They go in front of it: ti chiamo.

right.en: Maria never says hello to me.

contrasts.why: Nothing comes between the pronoun and the verb. Non stands before the pair: non mi saluta.

contrasts.wrong: Hai visto Paolo? Sì, ho lo visto ieri.

right.tl: Hai visto Paolo? Sì, l'ho visto ieri.
right.en: Have you seen Paolo? Yes, I saw him yesterday.

contrasts.why: In the passato prossimo the pronoun goes before avere, not between avere and the participle: l'ho visto.

contrasts.wrong: Dov'è Luca? Aspetto per lui da un'ora.

right.tl: Dov'è Luca? Lo aspetto da un'ora.
right.en: Where is Luca? I have been waiting for him for an hour.

contrasts.why: Aspettare takes a direct object: aspetto Luca, with no per. So wait for him is lo aspetto.

contrasts.wrong: Dov'è il mio telefono? Lo ecco, è sul divano.

right.tl: Dov'è il mio telefono? Eccolo, è sul divano.
right.en: Where is my phone? Here it is, it is on the sofa.

contrasts.why: Ecco is not a conjugated verb. The pronoun is attached to its end in one word: eccolo.

right.en: We will do the shopping tomorrow.

contrasts.why: The pronoun that repeats a fronted object has the form of that noun. La spesa is feminine singular, so la, not lo.

cheat: Copy the noun: il → lo, la → la, i / gli → li, le → le. Things too.
Pronoun before the conjugated verb, non before the pronoun: non lo conosco.
Passato prossimo: before avere. L'ho visto, li ho visti, never ho lo visto.
l' only for lo and la: l'ho letto. Li and le stay whole: li ho letti.
It meaning a fact or an idea: lo. Lo so, non lo capisco.
No preposition: lo aspetto, la ascolto, li cerco, la guardo, lo pago.
Ecco + pronoun, one word: eccolo, eccomi. Object first: il pane lo compro io.
